title: Lab 220: Linux User Management — Advanced
description: The objective of this lab is to develop practical skills in managing Linux users, groups, UIDs, GIDs, primary groups, supplementary groups, passwd lock and unlock, and user account removal.

lab_objective.description: The objective of this lab is to develop practical skills in managing local Linux users and groups.
objectives: Configure primary and supplementary group membership.
Verify account configuration using standard Linux commands.
scenario:
You are a Linux system administrator responsible for preparing and maintaining user accounts for a newly formed Infrastructure Operations Team.

The team contains application engineers, database administrators, and Linux support personnel.

During the account setup process, the requirements change several times. You must create the accounts, assign appropriate group memberships, modify existing accounts, enforce password policies, temporarily disable an account, rename accounts and groups, and finally retire some accounts.

tasks.title: Create the Lab Directory and Groups
steps: Create lab220_user_mgt directory inside your home directory
Store the verification output for every task inside /home/your-user-name/lab220_user_mgt/ directory
Create the following groups with the specified GIDs:
Verify all four groups using getent group.

tasks.title: Create Users with Specific UIDs
steps: Each user should have a normal home directory.

tasks.title: Configure Supplementary Groups
steps: Configure supplementary group membership for the following users as follows:
Add engineers to max's supplementary groups.
Add support to max's supplementary groups without removing any existing supplementary groups.
Add platform to smith's supplementary groups.
Add database to smith’s supplementary groups without removing any existing supplementary groups.
Add engineers to sarah's supplementary groups.
Add platform to sophia's supplementary groups.
Add database to sophia’s supplementary groups without removing any existing supplementary groups.
Do not change the users' primary groups.
Important: Do not accidentally replace existing supplementary group memberships while adding a new group.
Hint: Think carefully about the difference between usermod –G and usermod -aG
Verify all four users using id users.

tasks.title: Add and Remove Supplementary Memberships
steps: Remove David from the database supplementary group.
Add Maria to the support supplementary group.
Remove Sophia from the database supplementary group.
Do not change any user's primary group.
Verify all three accounts using id.

tasks.title: Set Passwords for Existing Users
steps: Use the passwd command to set a password for the following users:
Password choice is yours. You may choose any password you prefer.
Do not place passwords in any verification file.
Verify that each account has password information configured using appropriate account-management commands.
Important: Never record the actual passwords in the lab output.

tasks.title: Lock a User Account
steps: Maria will be temporarily unavailable for several weeks.
Verify that Maria's account is locked using an appropriate command.

tasks.title: Unlock an Existing User Account
steps: Maria has returned to the team.
Hint: Use passwd with the appropriate account-unlock option.
Verify that Maria's account is no longer locked.

tasks.title: Remove Users from Supplementary Groups
steps: Remove Alex from support and engineers.
Remove Maria from support and engineers.
Do not change their primary groups.

tasks.title: Delete an Unused Group
steps: The database group is no longer required.
1. Verify that no user requires it as a primary group.
2. Remove any remaining supplementary memberships if necessary.

tasks.title: Delete Temporary User
steps: Delete the sophia account and its home directory.
- sophia no longer exists. Verify id sophia

tasks.title: Final Account Cleanup
steps: The platform and support groups are no longer required.
Before deleting them, verify that no remaining user has them as a primary or supplementary group.

completion_message: Congratulations! You have completed Lab 220 - Linux User Management - Advances. You created and managed Linux users and groups, assigned specific UIDs and GIDs, configured primary and supplementary group memberships, locked and unlocked users password, removed users from supplementary groups, deleted groups, and safely removed user accounts. You also verified account configuration using standard Linux commands.
